claims.statement: playRandomQueue filters playable songs, applies mood-slot candidate filtering when active, delegates to RandomQueuePlanner.planRandomQueue, and on success exits infinite mode, replaces the in-memory recent-played set with the plan's, and starts the batch via setPlayQueue(plan.songs, 0, PlayMode.SEQUENTIAL); it returns false and starts nothing when no songs are playable.

RandomQueuePlanner batches by neededSize = minOf(DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=20, playable pool size), excludes recentSongIds from selection, and when the remainder falls below the batch it clears the recent set (resetHistory=true) and reuses the whole pool; trimToLimit caps the returned recent set to the playable library size, dropping earliest-inserted ids first. With uniform random off the selection is shuffle(pool).take(batch) shuffled again.

UniformRandomPlanner.selectSongs groups candidates by raw play count (playCounts[id] ?: 0) into ascending tiers — tier 0 = smallest-count group, tier 1 = next, remaining groups flattened as fallback — and fills the quota by tier priority with in-tier shuffling, never crossing into higher tiers while a lower tier has songs. Thresholds derive from the current distribution, so tiering survives when every song has been played past any fixed threshold, and equal counts degenerate to a single tier (pure shuffle). With the flag off it plain-shuffles.

UniformRandomPlanner.orderSongs and buildPlayOrderIds provide count-tiered play-mode ordering (current song first for SHUFFLE), but production wiring installs QueueManager.defaultPlayOrderBuilder in app/di/PlayerModule, so the SHUFFLE play mode stays pure shuffle and independent of uniform random; the tiered builders are the prepared bodies should the PlayOrderBuilder seam ever become settings-aware.

The uniform-random switch is carried on PlayerUiState.globalUniformRandomEnabled (default true), persisted by PlayerSettingsRepository (DataStore with legacy-SharedPreferences fallback true), loaded into UI state at PlayerRuntime.start(), and toggled from Settings via setGlobalUniformRandomEnabled. Changing the setting only writes the flag — it never reshuffles the live queue or its playOrderIds; it takes effect on the next random selection, infinite refill batch, or future queue rebuild.

PlayerRandomQueueFacade receives play counts through an injected rawPlayCounts callable (default empty); PlayerRuntime wires it to PlayStatsRepository.getRawPlayCounts (Room-backed raw play count, distinct from the effective count used for sorting), and both playRandomQueue and refillInfinitePlayQueue query it per candidate pool at call time.

startInfinitePlay keeps the current queue untouched: planInfiniteStart only records the queued playable song ids as the infinitePlayedSongIds coverage set, and an empty queue is legal (mode starts armed, waiting for refills). If the controller is already near the tail (remainingMediaItems() <= 5) it refills immediately, so the next track (natural end or system media keys) is a new song instead of a REPEAT_MODE_ALL wrap back to the old window's first item.

Infinite-queue refills are triggered by PlayerMediaEventFacade.handleMediaItemEnded (fires on every track transition; refills when wrapped or remaining <= DEFAULT_REFILL_THRESHOLD=5, passing advanceAfterWrap=wrapped) and by PlayerPlaybackFacade.playNext when planNext returns RefillInfiniteQueue; a pending skipNextRefill (set by add-to-next) is consumed instead of refilling so an inserted next song is not pushed back.

planInfiniteRefill sizes the batch like lucky play, excludes both the coverage set (playedSongIds) and songs already in the queue, clears the coverage set with resetHistory=true when the unplayed remainder is below the batch, and always selects through UniformRandomPlanner (the flag decides tiered vs plain shuffle); empty selection leaves the queue untouched, otherwise songs are appended via PlayQueue.withSongs which preserves the current item's index.

PlaybackController detects a window-tail wrap by index (isMediaItemWrap: new index 0 and previous index was the last item) rather than by transition reason, because Media3 reports a REPEAT_MODE_ALL tail wrap as SEEK (manual) or AUTO (natural end) while MEDIA_ITEM_TRANSITION_REASON_REPEAT only means single-item repeat; AUTO/SEEK/REPEAT transitions all route to onMediaItemEnded, so headset/lock-screen/notification skips also refill infinite mode.

On refill after a wrap (advanceAfterWrap=true), the facade sets the business queue's current index to the pre-append queue length — the first newly appended song — and starts it through playFromQueue (error-checked queue start) instead of syncPlayerQueue, so the user hears new songs rather than the replayed old window; when no new songs were added it keeps the current song and neither plays nor syncs.

Mood time-slot filtering happens at the planner entry, not inside the planners: when the slot is active, filterByMoodTags narrows the candidate pool to songs whose emotion tags intersect the slot's tags, and tiered selection plus recent eviction are reused unchanged on that pool (uniform random composes); an empty filtered pool logs 'fall back to full library' and returns null so playback falls back to full-library random, and pools below MoodSlotPolicy.POOL_WARN_THRESHOLD=10 log a loop warning. Slot configs and emotion tags are Volatile snapshots on PlayerRuntime with an injectable nowMinuteOfDay.

The lucky-play and infinite-play entry wiring lives in the app shell, not AppNavHost: NowPlayingSurface wires onLuckyPlayClick→PlayerViewModel.playRandomQueue() and onStartInfinitePlay→PlayerViewModel.startInfinitePlay(), AppRoot duplicates the lucky-play wiring for the empty-queue LuckyPlayEntryBar, and HomeRouteActions (feature/home) provides a pair with simpler generic toasts. On success each reads currentMoodSlotName() and, when a slot is active, shows the mood attribution toast — '已按「$slotName」为你随机播放' for lucky play (failure shows the import hint '还没有可播放的音乐，请先导入歌曲吧~') and '已按「$slotName」开启无限随机播放' for infinite start; both actions also reset the playlist-resume source via playlistResumeViewModel.switchSource(null, ...). currentMoodSlotName() delegates to PlayerRuntime.currentMoodSlot()→PlayerRandomQueueFacade.currentMoodSlot(), the same activeMoodSlot() evaluation the random decision used, so the attribution can never disagree with the applied filter.

Lucky-play eviction history (recentPlayedSongIds) is in-memory only and resets with the process, while isInfinitePlay and infinitePlayedSongIds are persisted through PlaybackStateStore (IS_INFINITE_PLAY / INFINITE_PLAYED_IDS alongside the queue JSON) and restored with saved played-ids filtered to songs still in the library (an empty queue may restore while infinite mode is on via allowEmpty=isInfinitePlay), so infinite play survives process death. PlayerPersistenceFacade.savePlaybackStateAsync captures the position and full state snapshot on the caller thread and only then moves the DataStore write to IO via launchIo, threading the up-front position into the snapshot so an IO save cannot read a stale position or a mid-save swapped queue; PlaybackStateStore.save also skips writing an empty-session queue JSON that would clobber an existing snapshot. Infinite mode exits via stopInfinitePlay, via setPlayQueue's default exitInfinitePlay=true, or explicitly in playRandomQueue; playRelatedSongs is the exception that keeps it on, re-seeding infinitePlayedSongIds with the new current+related queue so refills reach outside it.

The random chain is locked by tests that must stay green before changing it: RandomQueuePlannerTest (eviction, resetHistory, uniform selection after filtering, infinite start/refill exclusions), UniformRandomPlannerTest (tier preemption, dynamic tiering beyond fixed thresholds, equal-count degeneration, orderSongs grouping), PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest (start/refill/wrap semantics and the mood-filter scenarios including uniform compatibility), PlayerMediaEventFacadeTest (tail and wrap refill triggers), and MediaItemWrapDetectionTest (index-based wrap rule edge cases).
